rawInput.answer: Routes are registered via RouterGroup methods (GET/POST/etc. in routergroup.go, e.g. handle() at line 86) which call Engine.addRoute (gin.go:364), inserting the path into a per-HTTP-method radix tree (methodTrees, one *node root per method) via node.addRoute (tree.go:135). Incoming requests are matched in Engine.ServeHTTP -> handleHTTPRequest (gin.go:662,690), which looks up the tree for the request's method and calls root.getValue(path, ...) (tree.go:418), a radix-tree traversal that walks path segments/indices/wildcards to find matching handlers and extract params, falling back to trailing-slash redirect, 405, or 404 handling if no match.

rawInput.answer:
Params like `:name` are recognized at route-registration time by findWildcard (tree.go:253), which scans a path segment for a leading `:` (param) or `*` (catch-all) and returns the wildcard token (e.g. ":name") plus its start index. node.insertChild (tree.go:288) uses this to split the tree: it creates a child node with nType=param, path=":name" (colon retained) and sets the parent's wildChild=true; this param node is always kept as the last entry in n.children.

During matching, node.getValue (tree.go:418) walks the tree by literal prefix/index matching until it hits a node with wildChild=true, at which point it descends into the wildcard child via `n = n.children[len(n.children)-1]` (tree.go, ~line 484). For an `nType == param` node, it scans the remaining request path up to the next `/` (or end of string) to find the segment (`end` loop), extracts `path[:end]` as the value (optionally URL-unescaping it), and appends `Param{Key: n.path[1:], Value: val}` to the params slice — `n.path[1:]` strips the leading `:` so the key is just `name`. For `nType == catchAll` nodes the entire remaining path is captured as the value with `Key: n.path[2:]` (stripping the leading `/*`). Captured params are accumulated in a preallocated `Params` slice (`c.params`/`value.params`) sized via `engine.maxParams`, and skippedNode bookkeeping lets the walker backtrack past a wildcard branch to try static siblings first, undoing any params recorded past that point via `paramsCount`.

report.answer:
Params like `:name` are recognized at route-registration time by findWildcard (tree.go:253), which scans a path segment for a leading `:` (param) or `*` (catch-all) and returns the wildcard token (e.g. ":name") plus its start index. node.insertChild (tree.go:288) uses this to split the tree: it creates a child node with nType=param, path=":name" (colon retained) and sets the parent's wildChild=true; this param node is always kept as the last entry in n.children.

During matching, node.getValue (tree.go:418) walks the tree by literal prefix/index matching until it hits a node with wildChild=true, at which point it descends into the wildcard child via `n = n.children[len(n.children)-1]` (tree.go, ~line 484). For an `nType == param` node, it scans the remaining request path up to the next `/` (or end of string) to find the segment (`end` loop), extracts `path[:end]` as the value (optionally URL-unescaping it), and appends `Param{Key: n.path[1:], Value: val}` to the params slice — `n.path[1:]` strips the leading `:` so the key is just `name`. For `nType == catchAll` nodes the entire remaining path is captured as the value with `Key: n.path[2:]` (stripping the leading `/*`). Captured params are accumulated in a preallocated `Params` slice (`c.params`/`value.params`) sized via `engine.maxParams`, and skippedNode bookkeeping lets the walker backtrack past a wildcard branch to try static siblings first, undoing any params recorded past that point via `paramsCount`.
